chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not cut off your kinship, even if they cut you off.'
ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about maintaining family ties when relatives cut you off?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on *silat al-rahim* as a proactive duty rather than a reciprocal arrangement, reflecting the Imams' teaching that kinship ties are anchored in blood relation regardless of social reciprocity. It underscores the ethical ideal of *ihsan* (excellence) in family relations, urging believers to initiate reconciliation even when others have severed ties, thereby preventing the cycle of estrangement. This principle is central to maintaining social cohesion and spiritual purity in Shia jurisprudence and ethics.
